issues.legal_issue: An institution that began as a charity may become an industry when its later activities include organized, employee-supported production and substantial sale of goods beyond its own needs.
material_facts: The institution began as a charitable animal-care organization but later maintained and bred cattle, including through the use of stud bulls.
A substantial number of employees attended to the cattle, milked them, and carried and sold the milk to the public.
The milk sales generated substantial income and greatly exceeded the value of milk supplied to sick and infirm animals.
The institution’s workers raised a dispute about wages and service benefits, which was referred for adjudication to an Industrial Tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The institution’s activities constituted an industry within the meaning of section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(j), the character of the activity is central: systematic production or distribution of goods, or rendering of material services, through employer-employee cooperation may constitute an industry. A profit motive is not essential, but charitable origins alone do not determine the character of later activities; the activity must be assessed on its actual organization and economic character. The Court considered State of Bombay v. Hospital Mazdoor Sabha, Safdar Jung Hospital v. K. S. Sethi, Lalit Hari Ayurvedic College Pharmacy v. Its Workers’ Union, the Madras Panjrapole decisions, Gymkhana Club Union v. Management, Cricket Club v. Labour Union, and Harinagar Cane Farm v. State of Bihar.

rule.if: industrial_dispute_reference and systematic_goods_production and employee_cooperation and substantial_market_sales and production_beyond_internal_needs

predicates.industrial_dispute_reference: Workers raised an employment dispute that was referred to an adjudicative tribunal.
predicates.systematic_goods_production: The institution regularly maintained and bred cattle and produced milk.
predicates.employee_cooperation: Employees cared for the cattle, milked them, and handled the milk for sale.
predicates.substantial_market_sales: The institution sold a substantial quantity of milk to members of the public.
predicates.production_beyond_internal_needs: The value and quantity of milk sold substantially exceeded what the institution used for its own animals.

issues.definition: When an industrial-dispute reference concerns an institution that systematically produces goods with employee cooperation and sells substantial output beyond its own needs, the institution is an industry.
